test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (JSO) 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Index numbers are used to indicate changes in ______ over a specified time.

options.text: measures of central tendency and dispersion
prices, sales, industrial production, imports and exports of different commodities, cost of living, etc.

solution:
The correct answer is** prices, sales, industrial production, imports and exports of different commodities, cost of living, etc.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Index numbers are used to indicate changes in prices, sales, industrial production, imports and exports of different commodities, cost of living, etc.:**

 
 
• Index numbers are statistical measures designed to show changes in variables or groups of related variables over time.
 
• They are crucial in financial enterprises for tracking economic performance, inflation, and other economic indicators.
 
• Examples include the Consumer Price Index (CPI), Producer Price Index (PPI), and stock market indices like the S&P 500.
 
• These indices help businesses, investors, and policymakers make informed decisions by providing a clear picture of economic trends.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Measures of central tendency and dispersion:**

 
 
• These are statistical tools used to summarize data, such as mean, median, mode (central tendency), and range, variance, standard deviation (dispersion).
 
• They are not typically used for indicating changes over time but rather for describing the distribution of data at a single point in time.
 
 
 
• **Correlation and regression analysis:**
 
 
• These are statistical methods used to examine the relationship between two or more variables.
 
• While they can show trends or relationships, they do not directly indicate changes over time like index numbers do.
 
 
 
• **Skewness and kurtosis:**
 
 
• These are measures of the shape of the distribution of data.
 
• Skewness measures the asymmetry, while kurtosis measures the peakedness of the distribution.
 
• They are more about the characteristics of the data distribution rather than changes over time.
